I am a 35-year-old farmer with 5 years under my belt here in Quzhou. I know this land, and I know cabbage. With 50 mu and well water, I can manage three crops a year if I plan tight. My family of four gives me the hands I need at planting and harvest, so I do not hire much outside labor.

Here is how I see this year:

**Spring Cabbage (50 mu, early season):** I will plant hybrid spring cabbage varieties in late February under plastic mulch to warm the soil. Cabbage is my cash crop and I cannot afford low yields, so hybrid seed is worth the extra cost. I will rotary till the fields first to break up the soil and mix in my base fertilizer. I will put down about 25 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, and 12 kg potassium per mu—half as basal, half as top-dressing when the heads start forming. I will irrigate 6 times because spring can be dry here, and spray pesticides 3 times to keep cabbage worms and aphids off. I expect around 3,500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

**Summer Cabbage (50 mu, mid season):** As soon as the spring cabbage is out in late May, I will till again and put in heat-tolerant hybrid cabbage. Summer is harder—the heat stresses the plants—so I will increase irrigation to 8 times, watering early morning or evening to reduce evaporation. Fertilizer will stay about the same, maybe 25-10-12, but I will apply it quicker because the crop grows fast, about 60 days. Pesticides go up to 4 times because summer pests are worse. I expect a bit less yield, maybe 3,200 kg per mu, but prices are usually good in midsummer.

**Autumn Cabbage (50 mu, late season):** This is my main and best crop. I will plant in early August after the summer harvest, rotary till again, and use the same hybrid varieties that store well. Autumn weather on the North China Plain is perfect for cabbage—cool days, warm sun—so I expect my highest yields, around 4,500 kg per mu. I will cut irrigation back to 5 times since there is usually some rain, and spray 3 times for pests. Fertilizer stays at 25-10-12. I will harvest in November before hard frost and either sell fresh or store in my cellar if prices are low.

I stick with rotary tillage every season because my soil compacts easily and no-tillage does not work well for fine-seeded cabbage here. I trust what I have learned over these 5 years.
